source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 5–6. All 58 exact original records are hashed, with no note elements in this scope. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves both sexes and the special vow, connects Nazirite with separation, and uses inclusive pronouns for the explicitly mixed referent.
Preserves wine, shekhar, both vinegars, the uncertain grape-soaking drink and fresh/dried grapes rather than reducing the rule to alcohol alone.
Keeps the razor image, duration, holiness and uncut hair without making the vow male-only.
Keeps all four close relationships and the costly restriction, preserving the head/consecration image for explanation in the note.
Keeps the doubled suddenness, involuntary defilement, consecrated head and repeated shaving instruction with the exact day.
Retains sin and atonement terminology in the involuntary corpse case, both distinct offerings and same-day reconsecration; does not assign an unstated final-clause agent.
Keeps restarting the full period, year-old male lamb, guilt offering and lost prior days with the stated reason.
Uses passive for the unspecified bringer, retaining completion and sanctuary entrance rather than silently changing the Hebrew to self-arrival.
Preserves number, age, animal sex, freedom from defect and each distinct offering assignment.
Keeps location, the consecrated head, removed hair and fire beneath the sacrifice; does not put the hair on a different altar or discard it.
Keeps vowed offering, additional means and fulfillment of the actual vow without reducing the obligation to a suggested contribution.
Preserves the divine face and shining image, grace and second invocation of the LORD; lineation follows the two clauses.
Keeps the repeated face image and lifting rather than replacing it with an explanation, ending in shalom with its breadth noted.
Preserves the name-placement image, priestly plural they and emphatic divine I rather than attributing blessing solely to the priests.
